title: Developer Experience: SDK Guides, Quickstarts & Top Support Issues (Playbook)
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview:

This playbook codifies developer-experience (DevEx) guidance for SDK guides, quickstarts, reusable templates, API examples, docs-site operating procedures, and canonical fixes for the top support issues we see in the field. It is intended for SDK authors, developer docs writers, support engineers, and product/engineering owners who ship and maintain developer-facing docs and sample code.

Goals:
- Provide a consistent, high-quality structure for SDK documentation and quickstarts so engineers can get started in <30 minutes.
- Centralize canonical API examples and known-good configurations to reduce variance in support answers.
- Maintain an ops playbook for the docs site: PR process, versioning, release cadence, and rollback steps.
- Capture top support issues and step-by-step canonical fixes to reduce mean-time-to-resolution.

Audience:
- SDK maintainers (Python, Node.js, Go)
- Developer docs engineers and technical writers
- Developer support and solutions engineers
- Developer advocates and sample-app owners

Ownership and Contacts:
- Owner: eng-developer-experience (Primary contact: Aisha Patel)
- Secondary owners: SDK Owners (team leads for python-sdk, node-sdk)
- Support escalation: developer-support@redwood.ai

Structure of this document:
1) Recommended SDK guide structure
2) Quickstarts & template inventory
3) API examples (canonical)
4) Docs site operating procedures (PR, release, rollback)
5) Top support issues & canonical fixes
6) Onboarding checklist and metrics

1) Recommended SDK guide structure
- Title and 1-line summary
- Prerequisites: environment, account, permissions, API key scope
- Install: exact pip/npm/go get command with pinned minimum version
- Authentication: how to set REDWOOD_API_KEY, KMS guidance if applicable
- Minimal example: copy-paste runnable snippet (<=12 lines)
- Walkthrough: explain each call, common options, error handling
- Advanced usage: streaming, function/tool calling, embeddings, batching
- Configuration reference: table of options and defaults
- Troubleshooting: top 5 errors and quick fixes
- Tests & CI: how to run SDK unit tests and linting
- Changelog and compatibility notes

2) Quickstarts & template inventory (canonical templates)
Use this table to pick the right starting point. Add new templates via PR to /confluence/eng-developer-experience/quickstarts-and-templates and update the table below.

Name | Path (repo or doc) | Owner | Use-case | Last-updated
-----|--------------------|-------|----------|-----------
Python minimal text generation | /quickstarts/python-text-gen.md | python-sdk | Minimal serverless demo | 2025-06-02
Node.js chat sample | /quickstarts/node-chat.md | node-sdk | Chat + function calling | 2025-07-14
Embedding search (Python) | /quickstarts/embeddings-search.md | python-embeddings | Vector search starter | 2025-05-20
Realtime streaming demo | /quickstarts/streaming-demo.md | devrel | Streaming + SSE | 2025-03-18
Template: API example snippets set | /templates/api-snippets-collection.md | devex | Canonical snippets for support | 2025-08-01

Notes on templates:
- Each quickstart must include a small sample app, tests, and an automated smoke-test (see section "Docs site CI rules").
- Templates are stored as markdown in the docs repo and must reference the canonical API versions (pinned in configs/versions.yaml).

3) API examples (canonical)
All examples below are authoritative. Support teams should reference these in replies and link to them from internal KB. Keep examples minimal and focused on one feature. Include both synchronous and streaming examples where applicable.

A) Minimal text generation (Python)
```python
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.environ["REDWOOD_API_KEY"])
resp = client.generate("Write a 2-line haiku about latency")
print(resp.text)
```
Notes: use RedwoodClient.generate for simple cases. For chat, prefer client.chat with messages param.

B) Node.js chat + function calling
```javascript
const { RedwoodClient } = require('@redwood/inference')
const client = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY })
const resp = await client.chat({ messages: [{role: 'user', content: 'Get me the current exchange rate'}], tools: [/* tool definitions */] })
console.log(resp.output)
```

C) Curl example (quick troubleshooting)
```bash
curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"rw-mid-13b","input":"Summarize: ..."}'
```

D) Embeddings + vector upsert (Python)
```python
from redwood import EmbeddingsClient
emb = EmbeddingsClient(api_key=os.environ['REDWOOD_API_KEY'])
v = emb.create("The quick brown fox")
# upsert vector v into customer's vector DB (example uses our managed vector store client)
```

4) Docs site operating procedures
- Docs branch strategy:
  - main: production content (published site)
  - release/*: scheduled content releases (quarterly syncs with SDK releases)
  - patch/*: hotfixes to examples or security-sensitive docs
- PR checklist (required for merge):
  1) Author has validated examples locally and in the docs-preview environment.
  2) Linting passes: markdownlint, spellcheck, linkcheck.
  3) Smoke-test results attached (screenshot or CI pass link).
  4) Reviewer from SDK team assigned and has approved.
  5) If changing API contract, add note to release notes and notify support.
- Docs CI rules:
  - Every quickstart must have a smoke-test in CI that runs the minimal example against a test API key (secrets-masked).
  - Examples using streaming must have a fallback (non-streaming) example for CI smoke-tests.
- Release process:
  1) Cut release branch from main for docs release.
  2) Run full linkcheck and smoke tests.
  3) Merge and trigger site build.
  4) Monitor docs site build health for 30 minutes post-deploy (pager duty if build fails).
- Rollback procedure:
  - Revert the merge commit on main, re-run build. Contact platform-docs@redwood.ai and SRE if the rollback affects site routing.

5) Top support issues and canonical fixes (canonical KB for support replies)
This section contains the most frequent issues reported by customers and the canonical step-by-step fixes. Support engineers must reference these in ticket responses and link to the relevant quickstart or code snippet.

Issue A: Authentication errors (401/invalid_api_key)
- Symptoms: curl returns 401, SDK raises InvalidAPIKeyError
- Root causes: expired key, wrong environment variable name, key scoped for embeddings only, missing Bearer prefix in manual tools
- Canonical fix steps:
  1) Verify environment variable: echo $REDWOOD_API_KEY (ensure no extra whitespace).
  2) Confirm the key is active in Console > API keys.
  3) If using SDK, ensure you pass api_key or set REDWOOD_API_KEY. Example: export REDWOOD_API_KEY="sk_live_..."
  4) For restricted keys (embeddings-only), regenerate a general-purpose key or use the appropriate client.
  5) If issue persists, collect request_id from logs and escalate to eng-sre.

Issue B: Streaming responses truncated or timeout
- Symptoms: client receives partial stream then connection closes; server shows 499 or EOF
- Root causes: intermediate proxies closing idle connections, client-side read buffer not consuming fast enough, incorrect SSE header on proxies
- Canonical fix steps:
  1) Validate network path: curl --no-buffer against the streaming endpoint and confirm SSE events.
  2) Add keep-alive / ping messages in client for long-lived streams.
  3) Check load balancer/proxy timeout; raise to >= 120s for streaming ops.
  4) If using our SDK, update to the latest streaming helper (>= v1.4.0) that handles reconnects.

Issue C: High latency on small requests (tails)
- Symptoms: 95th latency much higher than median for short prompts
- Root causes: batching strategy configured suboptimally, model cold-start, prefix cache miss
- Canonical fix steps:
  1) Check request headers for batching hints and route.
  2) For production, set preferred model variant or pin to a dedicated pool.
  3) Enable prefix/KV cache for repetitive warm prompts.
  4) If observed on a dedicated plan, open a capacity investigation with eng-sre.

Issue D: Embeddings mismatch for vector search
- Symptoms: Search results irrelevant after SDK upgrade
- Root causes: model or tokenizer change, mismatched vector dimensionality, unnormalized vectors
- Canonical fix steps:
  1) Confirm embeddings model version used for both upsert and query (must match).
  2) Verify dimensionality and normalization steps in client code.
  3) Reindex corpus if model changed.

Issue E: Example code fails CI due to new lint rules
- Symptoms: CI fails with markdownlint or Python/Node linters after docs change
- Canonical fix steps:
  1) Run local linter: npm run lint or tox -e lint and fix reported issues.
  2) Update pre-commit config if the change is intentional and add a short note in PR.

6) Onboarding checklist for new SDK/docs contributors
- Read: this playbook and docs-site operating procedures
- Set up local docs preview environment (link to setup script in repo)
- Run smoke-tests for each quickstart template locally
- Pair with SDK owner for first PR review
- Add yourself to the CODEOWNERS file for the area you will maintain

7) Metrics and monitoring for docs & examples
- Track: number of broken links per release, smoke-test pass rate, average time-to-first-merge for quickstart PRs, number of support tickets referencing docs.
- Dashboards: docs-site CI failures (Grafana dashboard ID: docs-ci-01), support tickets by article (Zendesk tag: doc-article).

8) Future improvements (roadmap)
- Automated example runners for multiple SDK versions (matrix testing)
- Interactive quickstarts embedded in docs site (live sandboxes)
- Canonical example linter that verifies compatibility with pinned SDKs

Appendix: Useful CLI commands and checks
- Validate links: npm run linkcheck
- Run smoke tests: ./scripts/run-smoke-tests.sh --filter="python-text-gen"
- Lint docs: npm run lint:docs

Related policies and pages:
- Docs site operating procedures: /confluence/eng-developer-experience/docs-site/developer-experience-docs-site-operating-procedures-2026.json
- SDK release notes template: /confluence/eng-developer-experience/quickstarts-and-templates/sdk-release-notes-template.md

If anything in this playbook becomes outdated, open a PR and tag @devex for a review. For urgent support or incidents caused by docs (e.g., leaking secrets in examples), immediately contact the security on-call and change the affected examples to placeholders.
